title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 8
statement: Which of the cones below can be formed from a \(252^\circ\) sector of a circle of radius \(10\) by aligning the two straight sides?

solutions.text:
When the sector is rolled into a cone, its radius \(10\) becomes the slant height, and its arc becomes the base circle.

The arc length is \[ \dfrac{252}{360}\cdot 2\pi(10) = \dfrac{7}{10}\cdot 20\pi = 14\pi, \] so the base circumference is \(14\pi\) and the base radius is \(7.\)

The cone therefore has base radius \(7\) and slant height \(10,\) which is choice C.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The radius of the sector becomes the slant height of the cone, so the slant height is \(10\)
The arc length of the sector becomes the base circumference: \(\dfrac{252}{360}\cdot 2\pi(10)\)
